title: Ride Share Price Check
statement: A ride app keeps the last 200,000 fares in sorted order. Support wants to know whether any two fares add up to exactly a refund amount, to spot duplicate refunds.

approaches.name: Two pointers from both ends of the sorted fares
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The sort is already done; each step drops one fare.

approaches.name: A hash set of fares seen so far
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear, but ignores the order you already have and uses memory.

approaches.name: For each fare, binary search for refund − fare
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and fast enough, just slower than two pointers.

title: Server Alert Window
statement: A monitoring tool reads CPU load once a second for a day (86,400 readings). It must find the longest period in which the load stayed under the limit for all but at most 3 readings.
examples: Readings [ok, high, ok, ok, high, ok], at most 1 high → 4

approaches.name: Sliding window that tracks high readings inside it
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each reading enters and leaves the window once.

approaches.name: Prefix counts of high readings and binary search for each start
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, a bit slower and more memory.

approaches.name: DP over readings and allowed highs
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Works, but builds a table for a problem one window solves.

title: Warehouse Packing Speed
statement: A warehouse must pack 50,000 orders of different sizes within 10 hours, packing at most one order at a time. The manager wants the slowest packing speed (items per hour, a whole number) that still finishes in time.

approaches.name: Binary search on the speed, checking each speed with one pass
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: About 50,000 × 30 checks; if a speed works, every faster one does too.

approaches.name: Divide the total size by the hours
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Wrong: each order takes whole hours, so the average can be too slow.

approaches.name: Use a max-heap and always speed up for the largest order
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: No clear rule for when to stop; does not answer the question.
